title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：page　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 page 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the painter ① turned the page that no visitor in the studio would have counted, and he said the turning was the whole of the season. The ② page, meaning the sheet itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; a page, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ page in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ page at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A page, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the painter said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the page was the whole of the matter, meaning the story and not the sheet. The ⑥ page, meaning the story and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; page, he said, is either something you turn or the only word that means both a sheet and a story. He said the story is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ page had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ page of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of counting; page, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ page I remember is the sheet counted in the catalogue, which closed in 1962 and is still counted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ page, my mother said in 1964, is the only sheet that improves by being counted; every page, she said, is a story that has agreed to look like a sheet. She said the story was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 页；一页（指画室里每一页旁边的那一页）
B. n. 页；一页（指那页页本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：turn the page 翻这一页页
D. n. 页；一页（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 页之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的页之事）
F. n. 页；一页（指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一页）
G. n. 页、篇章（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 篇章（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: turned the page that no visitor in the studio would have counted
The page, meaning the sheet itself and not the brush
the page at the far easel
the page was the whole of the matter

The page of the whole thing
A page, my mother said in 1964

answers.why: turn the page 意为“翻这一页页”，1955 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯清点的一页页做了一遍。
page 意为“页；一页”，指那页页本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被清点。
page 意为“页；一页”，指画室里每一页旁边的那一页，每一页旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
page 意为“页；一页”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
page 意为“页、篇章”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这页篇章就是那件事的全部。
page 意为“篇章”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那页页，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
page 意为“页；一页”，指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一页，到 1960 年这一页成了展品目录里的一行。
page 意为“页之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的页之事是一处画室和三个季度的清点。
page 意为“页；一页”，我记得的是展品目录里清点过的那一页，1962 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一页。
page 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，页是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的页。
